h2: Nondestructive testing services by the names buyers use
html:
Buyers search for the same nondestructive testing services under several names, and US competitors list most methods twice, once as testing and once as inspection. This index uses the names you will see in US and Canadian purchase orders and points each one to the page that explains how we deliver it.

Conventional methods

  • Magnetic particle inspection (MPI), also written magnetic particle testing or MT: yoke, prod and coil techniques, visible or wet fluorescent, for surface and near-surface cracks in ferromagnetic steel.
  • Dye penetrant testing, also called liquid penetrant inspection, PT, or FPI when fluorescent: surface-breaking flaws on any non-porous material.
  • Ultrasonic testing (UT): thickness surveys and shear-wave weld examination.
  • Radiographic testing, also sold as industrial X-ray or radiography services: film, computed and digital radiography of welds and castings.
  • Visual testing (VT): the first method on every job, and the one most codes require on every weld.

Advanced methods

  • Phased array ultrasonic testing services (PAUT) and TOFD for encoded weld examination, crack sizing and corrosion mapping.
  • MFL inspection (magnetic flux leakage) for tank floors, with UT prove-up.
  • Heat exchanger inspection services: eddy current inspection, RFT and IRIS on tube bundles.
  • Pulsed eddy current through insulation, and ACFM for cracks under coatings.

How to buy non-destructive testing and inspection services

A good request for quotation names five things: the construction or in-service code (ASME Section VIII and B31.3 for new construction; API 510, 570 or 653 for equipment in service; AWS D1.1 for structural steel), the acceptance criteria, the procedure you require or will approve, the personnel certification you need, and the report format. In the US, technicians are usually certified by their employer to ASNT SNT-TC-1A or CP-189. On Canadian work, check whether the owner or the provincial regulator requires personnel certified by NRCan to CAN/CGSB-48.9712, and say so in the RFQ, because it changes who can be sent. Every Atlantis NDT report is reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III before release.

Choosing by damage, not by method

If you know the damage mechanism but not the method, start from the damage: wall loss calls for UT or corrosion mapping, surface cracking for MT or PT, buried weld flaws for RT or PAUT, and tube wall loss for eddy current or IRIS. The guide above sets out that choice in detail, and turnaround inspection services shows how the methods are combined during an outage. For a scope, send us the equipment list and the code.
